source.title: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
source.authors: Shengyuan Hu; Yi-Wei Fu; Steven Z. Wu; Virginia Smith

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether relearning can restore behavior after several unlearning methods, using keyword recovery, answer quality, and text-completion measures across several benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports relearning outcomes after unlearning and control results where relearning data is applied without unlearning. It also discusses in-context learning as a possible attack but says it was not verified. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks. Reported sweep curves are not fully numerically tabulated.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes unlearned models on small relearn sets: partial unlearn data, public or GPT-generated related text, and synthetic correlated tokens. It measures recovery of the targeted knowledge on TOFU, WHP and WMDP against unlearned baselines, with relearn-only controls. This is a different method aimed at whether unlearning removes knowledge or only suppresses it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that current approximate, finetuning-based unlearning methods simply suppress outputs rather than remove knowledge: benign relearning on small, loosely related or public data reverses unlearning. They note relearning success depends on data relatedness, unlearning method, model and metric (e.g. RMU: MCQ recovers, completion does not without layer reset). They recommend caution and better evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies relearning attacks after several unlearning baselines, rather than reproducing one original unlearning study's method and measure. It uses partial-set or public-text fine-tuning, and includes a separate synthetic correlated-token experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies with unlearning depth, number of relearning steps, relearn-text relevance and language, model, unlearning method, RMU layer knowledge, and evaluation metric. RMU recovery differs between MCQ accuracy and answer completion.
record.problems: Many results are shown only in plots or as selected examples; the paper gives no uncertainty estimates in the reported results. WMDP answer quality is judged by an LLM. The authors note that their WMDP relearn text may not always satisfy the no-answer condition despite filtering, and that model choice and evaluation metric affect conclusions.
record.rows_left_out: The full TOFU and WHP recovery curves across every unlearning checkpoint and relearning step are not separately transcribed because the text supplies only plotted values and a few aggregate statements; see Section 3, Figure 3, and Appendix J, Figure 8. The paper also reports retain-set MT-Bench scores in Appendix C.4, but those are capability checks rather than outcomes for the recovery versions. Additional WMDP per-method plotted values are represented by figure-only summaries in R7-R8.

untested.parts: Whether unlearned models keep general ability is not established. Retain MT-Bench scores (Fig 7) fall sharply for several methods, so some unlearned models may not meet A's precondition.
No activation-direction ablation. Evidence for blocking rather than deleting is only a toy synthetic token-pair analysis plus behavioural relearning.
Prompting-only attacks are not tested. The authors say in-context relearning is unverified; the same prompt is used before and after relearning.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: TOFU ASR after unlearning 30 steps then relearning: 10%, 40%, 30%, 20% at 15/30/48/60 steps, vs 0% for relearn-only
NLL on Mark falls as relearning lowers NLL on Anthony, though Mark is never trained (mechanistic evidence of retained association)
Table 4 rows for 1 pair repetition (0% at all relearn checkpoints) and shallow/medium checkpoint values
Per-method numeric values for Figures 4 and 5 (present in figure labels but not tabulated)

record.verdict_notes: RMU is one of A's original methods (WMDP), but this study is not an original source, so verdicts apply. MT-Bench retain scores (Fig 7) show several unlearned models lost much general ability, which weakens the inference that they met A's 'keeps general ability' condition. R15 is kept under B only. Plain relearning fails to restore RMU text completion, a setting where A largely holds for that attack.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests whether relearning attacks recover targeted behavior after unlearning, but does not establish near-chance targeted accuracy together with preserved general ability for every method and setting.
The paper tests relearning from partial unlearn data and loosely or generally related public text; it does not test every possible relearning-set size or composition.
The paper analyzes retained token associations in a simplified setting and tests resetting an RMU-corrupted layer followed by relearning. It does not test ablating an activation direction.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages used as prompts, or in-context information without weight updates. The paper notes that in-context learning was not verified.
A newer method presented as resisting the attacks in the claim. RMU is attacked in the paper; it is not presented as a counter-method.

relationships.condition: GA, GD, KL, NPO, SCRUB (full and LoRA), WHP alternate labels, and RMU MCQ, under benign relearning on TOFU, WHP and WMDP
relationships.reason: Small, non-answer-bearing relearn sets restore targeted outputs. Examples: WMDP judge score 1.27→6.2 (R3), LoRA GA/GD/NPO up to ~5.1–5.2 (R4–R6), RMU MCQ 0.31→0.48 (R14), keyword ASR >70% (R1–R2), HP verbatim recovery (R9, R12, R13).
relationships.display_finding: Small relearning sets containing no answers restored targeted outputs, raising WMDP judge scores from 1.27 to 6.2, LoRA scores to about 5.1–5.2, RMU MCQ accuracy from 0.31 to 0.48, and keyword attack success above 70%, alongside verbatim Harry Potter recovery.

relationships.condition: Deeper unlearning, too many relearn steps, weakly related or unrelated relearn text, weak token correlation, and RMU text completion
